llm.summary: This is a static Chinese lab-accreditation compliance checklist skill with no code, persistence, credential access, or hidden behavior.

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request local filesystem access, network access, credentials, external tools, or broad environment inspection.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only artifact/SKILL.md and no executable scripts, dependencies, remote loaders, or install-time behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions are scoped to user-submitted laboratory compliance documents and include a Chinese report template with blocking recommendations for severe noncompliance; the China-specific language is visible and purpose-aligned, though users wanting another language may need to ask explicitly.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No memory writes, background workers, privilege escalation, tool wrapping, scheduled tasks, or cross-session persistence are present.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is to review CMA, CNAS, ISO 17025, RB/T 214, personnel, equipment, environment, and publicity materials for laboratory qualification compliance; the artifact only provides checklist rules and a report format aligned with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Use this skill for Chinese laboratory qualification and accreditation drafting or review, but treat its compliance output as advisory and have qualified staff verify current legal and accreditation requirements before publication or submission.
llm.findings:
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese manifest description is consistent with a China-focused CMA/CNAS laboratory qualification workflow, so this is best treated as a localization note rather than a security concern.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese report template is visible in the artifact and matches the intended regulatory context; it does not add hidden authority or unsafe behavior.
